### GRI 302 Energy  
Shell’s total energy consumption in 2025 was 269 million MWh, down from 289 million MWh in 2024, primarily due to portfolio changes and greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement and transformation projects [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Of this, 189 million MWh was consumed from facilities under Shell’s operational control, with 187 million MWh (99%) sourced from fossil fuels — comprising 40 million MWh from crude oil and petroleum products, 108 million MWh from natural gas, 10 million MWh from other fossil sources, and 28 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from fossil sources [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Renewable energy consumption from facilities under operational control amounted to 2.6 million MWh in 2025, including 2.4 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from renewable sources [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Energy intensity per net revenue was 0.001 MWh/$ in both 2024 and 2025, though Shell notes this metric is not considered reliable for cross-entity or longitudinal comparison due to boundary misalignment between energy consumption (ESRS reporting boundary) and net revenue (financial control boundary) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828].

### GRI 303 Water  
Water consumption reported against the operational control boundary was 86 million cubic metres in 2025, down from 90 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_878]. Of this, approximately 72 million cubic metres (84%) was used for manufacturing oil products and chemicals, and 13 million cubic metres for oil and gas production [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_870]. In 2025, Shell consumed 8 million cubic metres of water in areas of high water stress, a reduction from 21 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Water recycled and reused totalled 25 million cubic metres in 2025, up from 23 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Shell retired its prior commitment to reduce fresh water consumption in water-stressed areas, having achieved it ahead of schedule in 2022; the commitment formally ended in December 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_876].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Shell’s gross Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (net of carbon credits) were 53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025, compared with 58 million tonnes CO₂e in 2024 and 83 million tonnes CO₂e in the 2016 baseline year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_204][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. This represents a 36% net reduction since 2016 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29]. The 2025 reduction was driven by divestments (4.8 million tonnes), emission-reduction activities and renewable electricity purchases (1.2 million tonnes), and changes in output (0.1 million tonnes), partially offset by acquisitions (1.4 million tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. Methane emissions intensity for Shell-operated oil and gas assets with marketed gas was 0.04% in 2025, well below the 0.2% target and trending toward near-zero by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]. Routine flaring from upstream operations was eliminated in January 2025, independent of the March 2025 sale of SPDC [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Shell generated 3,239 thousand tonnes of waste, down from 3,452 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Hazardous waste totalled 822 thousand tonnes (2024: 1,104 thousand tonnes), of which 615 thousand tonnes was directed to disposal (2024: 695 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Non-hazardous waste disposed was 1,533 thousand tonnes in 2025 (2024: 1,396 thousand tonnes), while hazardous waste disposed decreased to 454 thousand tonnes (2024: 536 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Total waste diverted from disposal was 403 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 728 thousand tonnes in 2024 — a decline attributed to changes in waste classification and reporting methodology [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Initiatives included using drilling waste in cement and lubricant production in Malaysia, trialling bio-sludge for soil enhancement in Qatar, and returning unused chemicals to suppliers in the Gulf of America [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_278][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_900].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Shell’s climate strategy is anchored in its ambition to become a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050 (Scope 1, 2 and 3), with interim targets aligned to a 1.5°C pathway derived from IPCC AR6 scenarios [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_222][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165]. Key metrics include net Scope 1 and 2 emissions (53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025), methane intensity (0.04% in 2025), routine flaring (eliminated in 2025), and Net Carbon Intensity (NCI) — reduced by 9.0% versus the 2016 baseline of 78 gCO₂e/MJ [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440]. Risk management integrates portfolio changes, abatement projects (e.g., CCS, electrification), and regulatory compliance, with carbon credits permitted only after avoidance and reduction, per the carbon mitigation hierarchy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223]. Targets are embedded in executive remuneration, including methane intensity and NCI performance [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440].

### Not covered in source material  
No quantitative data on Scope 3 emissions totals (Categories 1, 3, 9, 11) were provided in the context; only descriptions of methodology and category definitions were given. No water quality data (e.g., pollutant concentrations in discharges), biodiversity impact assessments, or detailed TCFD risk categorisation (e.g., physical vs transition risks) were disclosed. No waste-related targets beyond plastics packaging (30% recycled content by 2030) were specified.

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures in 2025, with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025 (unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8), resulting in an FPI frequency (FPI-F) of 2.1 cases per 100 million working hours, up from 1.7 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) was 1.2 per million working hours in 2025, compared to 1.1 in 2024; lost time injury frequency (LTIF) was 0.6 per million working hours in 2025, versus 0.5 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 and Mode 2 contract arrangements—where Shell retains control or shared interface management—but exclude Mode 3 contractors unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. Shell uses IOGP-defined FPI and FPI-F metrics to focus investigations on the most serious incidents and drive prevention of fatalities and permanent impairments [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This reflects a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily due to lower employee numbers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. Training supports skill development aligned with traditional and emerging business needs, including leadership development and coaching for executives [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260]. Ethics and compliance training—including mandatory Code of Conduct training—is required for all employees and contractor staff [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. For roles at higher risk of corruption or bribery, 98% of staff held valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training as of 2025 (consistent with 98% in 2024), with refresh cycles defined at two- to three-year intervals [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960].

### Diversity  
As of December 31, 2025, women comprised 35% of Shell’s total workforce of 85,000 employees [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Women represented 42% of the Board of Directors and 44% of the Executive Committee [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. In senior leadership positions (defined by compensation grade), women accounted for 35%—meeting Shell’s 2025 target—and the company aims for 40% by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. Ethnic minority representation in UK-based Senior Management stood at 16% in 2025, exceeding the Parker Review’s 15% target ahead of schedule; Shell now targets 17% by 2027 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. The Board included three Directors from minority ethnic backgrounds as of December 31, 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_495].

### Supplier Social Assessment  
Shell’s Supplier Principles require suppliers to uphold human rights—including freedom of association, elimination of forced and child labour, non-discrimination, safe working conditions, and fair wages—and to provide confidential grievance mechanisms for workers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_929]. Risk-based pre-contractual screening assesses supplier capacity to meet these expectations, and contracts require suppliers to flow down equivalent standards to their direct suppliers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. In 2025, no cases of non-respect of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines were identified in Shell’s upstream or downstream value chain [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. Additionally, no severe human rights incidents related to value chain workers were identified in 2025 (compared to three in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939].

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403: Specific occupational health metrics beyond safety (e.g., work-related illnesses, mental health support programmes, or exposure monitoring data) are not disclosed.  
GRI 404: Breakdown of training by topic (e.g., health and safety vs. technical skills), duration per employee, or participation rates for specific mandatory courses (beyond ethics/compliance) are not provided.  
GRI 405: Data on disability inclusion, LGBT+ representation, or intersectional diversity (e.g., gender and ethnicity combined) are absent.  
GRI 414: Quantitative details on supplier assessments conducted (e.g., number screened, percentage audited, or findings by risk category) are not reported.  
TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition): No explicit analysis of workforce transitions, reskilling for low-carbon roles, community impacts of portfolio changes (e.g., divestments in Nigeria, UK, Singapore), or just transition commitments is included in the provided context.

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures in 2025, with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025 (unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8), resulting in an FPI frequency (FPI-F) of 2.1 cases per 100 million working hours, up from 1.7 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) was 1.2 per million working hours in 2025, compared to 1.1 in 2024; lost time injury frequency (LTIF) was 0.6 per million working hours in 2025, versus 0.5 in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 and Mode 2 contract arrangements—where Shell retains control or shared interface management—but exclude Mode 3 contractors unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. Shell uses IOGP-defined FPI and FPI-F metrics to focus investigations on the most serious incidents and drive prevention of fatalities and permanent impairments [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This reflects a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily due to lower employee numbers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. Training supports skill development aligned with traditional and emerging business needs, including leadership development and coaching for executives [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260]. Ethics and compliance training—including mandatory Code of Conduct training—is required for all employees and contractor staff [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. For roles at higher risk of corruption or bribery, 98% of staff held valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training as of 2025 (consistent with 98% in 2024), with refresh cycles defined at two- to three-year intervals [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960].

### Diversity  
As of December 31, 2025, women comprised 35% of Shell’s total workforce of 85,000 employees [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Women represented 42% of the Board of Directors and 44% of the Executive Committee [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. In senior leadership positions (defined by compensation grade), women accounted for 35%—meeting Shell’s 2025 target—and the company aims for 40% by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. Ethnic minority representation in UK-based Senior Management stood at 16% in 2025, exceeding the Parker Review’s 15% target ahead of schedule; Shell now targets 17% by 2027 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. The Board included three Directors from minority ethnic backgrounds as of December 31, 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_495].

### Supplier Social Assessment  
Shell’s Supplier Principles require suppliers to uphold human rights—including freedom of association, elimination of forced and child labour, non-discrimination, safe working conditions, and fair wages—and to provide confidential grievance mechanisms for workers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_929]. Risk-based pre-contractual screening assesses supplier capacity to meet these expectations, and contracts require suppliers to flow down equivalent standards to their direct suppliers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. In 2025, no cases of non-respect of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines were identified in Shell’s upstream or downstream value chain [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. Additionally, no severe human rights incidents related to value chain workers were identified in 2025 (compared to three in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939].

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403: Specific occupational health metrics beyond safety (e.g., work-related illnesses, mental health support programmes, or exposure monitoring data) are not disclosed.  
GRI 404: Breakdown of training by topic (e.g., health and safety vs. technical skills), duration per employee, or participation rates for specific mandatory courses (beyond ethics/compliance) are not provided.  
GRI 405: Data on disability inclusion, LGBT+ representation, or intersectional diversity (e.g., gender and ethnicity combined) are absent.  
GRI 414: Quantitative details on supplier assessments conducted (e.g., number screened, percentage audited, or findings by risk category) are not reported.  
TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition): No explicit analysis of workforce transitions, reskilling for low-carbon roles, community impacts of portfolio changes (e.g., divestments in Nigeria, UK, Singapore), or just transition commitments is included in the provided context.

### Governance Structure and Board Oversight  
Shell plc’s governance framework is structured around the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee (EC), with the Board comprising 12 members—including two executive and 10 non-executive directors—as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 12 members, 2 executive and 10 non-executive members) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. All non-executive directors are considered independent in character and judgement, representing 83% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 83%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Board maintains primary oversight of Shell’s strategy—including its Energy Transition Strategy 2024, endorsed in March 2024—and monitors performance against longer-term business targets, including climate-related ambitions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Sustainability matters, including climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, are reviewed and addressed on an integrated basis alongside other business issues throughout the year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. The Board delegates authority for operational management to the CEO, who chairs the EC and is supported by EC members in implementing strategy and monitoring progress [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242].

### Board Diversity, Composition and Succession  
Shell’s Board Diversity Policy—first published in March 2024—commits to gender balance, with women constituting 42% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 42%), corresponding to a female-to-male ratio of 0.7 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Policy sets a target to maintain representation of both men and women at or above 40%, and aims to have at least one senior Board position (Chair, CEO, Senior Independent Director or CFO) held by a woman [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. Shell also aims to maintain or exceed having at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The Nomination and Succession Committee (NOMCO) oversees development of a diverse pipeline for Board succession and ensures all appointments follow a formal, rigorous and transparent procedure based on merit and objective criteria, with due regard for diversity factors [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. NOMCO engages independent executive search consultants aligned with Shell’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) approach to identify candidates from diverse pools [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379].

### Ethics, Compliance and Anti-Corruption Governance  
Accountability for ethics and compliance rests with the CEO and the Executive Committee, supported by the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO), who reports to the Chief Legal Officer and provides updates to the EC and Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Shell’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption programme includes mandatory Code of Conduct training for all employees and contractor staff, with targeted, risk-based training for roles involving procurement, government engagement or new business development [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. In 2025, 98% of staff in at-risk roles possessed valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training completion (2024: 98%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No Shell legal entity nor, to the best of Shell’s knowledge, any Shell staff were convicted or fined for criminal violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws in 2025 (2024: no convictions or fines) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961]. Breaches may be reported confidentially—including anonymously—via the Shell Global Helpline; in 2025, 1,983 reports were received [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. Shell maintains a stringent no-retaliation policy for good-faith reporters and those involved in investigations [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_956].

### Climate and Sustainability Risk Governance  
Climate change and the energy transition are identified as material strategic risks, with sub-components including commercial, societal (including litigation), regulatory and physical risks [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168]. The Board oversees climate-related risk management through dedicated structures: the Sustainability Committee addresses emerging sustainability trends (excluding carbon and safety); the Audit and Risk Committee reviews risk management effectiveness and internal controls; the Carbon Reporting Committee governs GHG emissions calculation and external disclosures; and the Sustainability Management Committee drives cross-business integration of sustainability objectives [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. The ARC assists the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities for risk management and internal control, including ethics and compliance-related matters [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Each business and function regularly reviews its risk profile and assurance activities to ensure climate-related risks are effectively managed, with insights informing operational decisions and risk response plans [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_783].

### Not covered in source material  
The provided context does not disclose: (i) specific quantitative metrics on Board meeting attendance or frequency; (ii) details of Board evaluation methodology beyond composition reviews; (iii) remuneration-linked ESG performance metrics for non-Executive Directors; (iv) third-party assurance scope or findings for governance disclosures; (v) board-level oversight of cyber-risk or data privacy governance; (vi) disclosure of political contributions or lobbying expenditures; (vii) detailed breakdown of committee mandates beyond high-level descriptions; (viii) whistleblower case resolution rates or investigation timelines.

### Governance Structure and Board Oversight  
Shell plc’s governance framework is structured around the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee (EC), with the Board comprising 12 members—including two executive and 10 non-executive directors—as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 12 members, 2 executive and 10 non-executive members) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. All non-executive directors are considered independent in character and judgement, representing 83% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 83%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Board maintains primary oversight of Shell’s strategy—including its Energy Transition Strategy 2024, endorsed in March 2024—and monitors performance against longer-term business targets, including climate-related ambitions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Sustainability matters, including climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, are reviewed and addressed on an integrated basis alongside other business issues throughout the year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. The Board delegates authority for operational management to the CEO, who chairs the EC and is supported by EC members in implementing strategy and monitoring progress [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242].

### Board Diversity, Composition and Succession  
Shell’s Board Diversity Policy—first published in March 2024—commits to gender balance, with women constituting 42% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 42%), corresponding to a female-to-male ratio of 0.7 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Policy sets a target to maintain representation of both men and women at or above 40%, and aims to have at least one senior Board position (Chair, CEO, Senior Independent Director or CFO) held by a woman [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. Shell also aims to maintain or exceed having at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The Nomination and Succession Committee (NOMCO) oversees development of a diverse pipeline for Board succession and ensures all appointments follow a formal, rigorous and transparent procedure based on merit and objective criteria, with due regard for diversity factors [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. NOMCO engages independent executive search consultants aligned with Shell’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) approach to identify candidates from diverse pools [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379].

### Ethics, Compliance and Anti-Corruption Governance  
Accountability for ethics and compliance rests with the CEO and the Executive Committee, supported by the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO), who reports to the Chief Legal Officer and provides updates to the EC and Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Shell’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption programme includes mandatory Code of Conduct training for all employees and contractor staff, with targeted, risk-based training for roles involving procurement, government engagement or new business development [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. In 2025, 98% of staff in at-risk roles possessed valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training completion (2024: 98%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No Shell legal entity nor, to the best of Shell’s knowledge, any Shell staff were convicted or fined for criminal violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws in 2025 (2024: no convictions or fines) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961]. Breaches may be reported confidentially—including anonymously—via the Shell Global Helpline; in 2025, 1,983 reports were received [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. Shell maintains a stringent no-retaliation policy for good-faith reporters and those involved in investigations [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_956].

### Climate and Sustainability Risk Governance  
Climate change and the energy transition are identified as material strategic risks, with sub-components including commercial, societal (including litigation), regulatory and physical risks [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168]. The Board oversees climate-related risk management through dedicated structures: the Sustainability Committee addresses emerging sustainability trends (excluding carbon and safety); the Audit and Risk Committee reviews risk management effectiveness and internal controls; the Carbon Reporting Committee governs GHG emissions calculation and external disclosures; and the Sustainability Management Committee drives cross-business integration of sustainability objectives [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. The ARC assists the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities for risk management and internal control, including ethics and compliance-related matters [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Each business and function regularly reviews its risk profile and assurance activities to ensure climate-related risks are effectively managed, with insights informing operational decisions and risk response plans [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_783].

### Not covered in source material  
The provided context does not disclose: (i) specific quantitative metrics on Board meeting attendance or frequency; (ii) details of Board evaluation methodology beyond composition reviews; (iii) remuneration-linked ESG performance metrics for non-Executive Directors; (iv) third-party assurance scope or findings for governance disclosures; (v) board-level oversight of cyber-risk or data privacy governance; (vi) disclosure of political contributions or lobbying expenditures; (vii) detailed breakdown of committee mandates beyond high-level descriptions; (viii) whistleblower case resolution rates or investigation timelines.

Environmental.draft:
### GRI 302 Energy  
Shell’s total energy consumption in 2025 was 269 million MWh, down from 289 million MWh in 2024, primarily due to portfolio changes and greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement and transformation projects [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Of this, 189 million MWh was consumed from facilities under Shell’s operational control, with 187 million MWh (99%) sourced from fossil fuels — comprising 40 million MWh from crude oil and petroleum products, 108 million MWh from natural gas, 10 million MWh from other fossil sources, and 28 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from fossil sources [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Renewable energy consumption from facilities under operational control amounted to 2.6 million MWh in 2025, including 2.4 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from renewable sources [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Energy intensity per net revenue was 0.001 MWh/$ in both 2024 and 2025, though Shell notes this metric is not considered reliable for cross-entity or longitudinal comparison due to boundary misalignment between energy consumption (ESRS reporting boundary) and net revenue (financial control boundary) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828].

### GRI 303 Water  
Water consumption reported against the operational control boundary was 86 million cubic metres in 2025, down from 90 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_878]. Of this, approximately 72 million cubic metres (84%) was used for manufacturing oil products and chemicals, and 13 million cubic metres for oil and gas production [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_870]. In 2025, Shell consumed 8 million cubic metres of water in areas of high water stress, a reduction from 21 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Water recycled and reused totalled 25 million cubic metres in 2025, up from 23 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Shell retired its prior commitment to reduce fresh water consumption in water-stressed areas, having achieved it ahead of schedule in 2022; the commitment formally ended in December 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_876].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Shell’s gross Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (net of carbon credits) were 53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025, compared with 58 million tonnes CO₂e in 2024 and 83 million tonnes CO₂e in the 2016 baseline year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_204][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. This represents a 36% net reduction since 2016 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29]. The 2025 reduction was driven by divestments (4.8 million tonnes), emission-reduction activities and renewable electricity purchases (1.2 million tonnes), and changes in output (0.1 million tonnes), partially offset by acquisitions (1.4 million tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. Methane emissions intensity for Shell-operated oil and gas assets with marketed gas was 0.04% in 2025, well below the 0.2% target and trending toward near-zero by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]. Routine flaring from upstream operations was eliminated in January 2025, independent of the March 2025 sale of SPDC [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Shell generated 3,239 thousand tonnes of waste, down from 3,452 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Hazardous waste totalled 822 thousand tonnes (2024: 1,104 thousand tonnes), of which 615 thousand tonnes was directed to disposal (2024: 695 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Non-hazardous waste disposed was 1,533 thousand tonnes in 2025 (2024: 1,396 thousand tonnes), while hazardous waste disposed decreased to 454 thousand tonnes (2024: 536 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Total waste diverted from disposal was 403 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 728 thousand tonnes in 2024 — a decline attributed to changes in waste classification and reporting methodology [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Initiatives included using drilling waste in cement and lubricant production in Malaysia, trialling bio-sludge for soil enhancement in Qatar, and returning unused chemicals to suppliers in the Gulf of America [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_278][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_900].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Shell’s climate strategy is anchored in its ambition to become a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050 (Scope 1, 2 and 3), with interim targets aligned to a 1.5°C pathway derived from IPCC AR6 scenarios [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_222][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165]. Key metrics include net Scope 1 and 2 emissions (53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025), methane intensity (0.04% in 2025), routine flaring (eliminated in 2025), and Net Carbon Intensity (NCI) — reduced by 9.0% versus the 2016 baseline of 78 gCO₂e/MJ [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440]. Risk management integrates portfolio changes, abatement projects (e.g., CCS, electrification), and regulatory compliance, with carbon credits permitted only after avoidance and reduction, per the carbon mitigation hierarchy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223]. Targets are embedded in executive remuneration, including methane intensity and NCI performance [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440].

### Not covered in source material  
No quantitative data on Scope 3 emissions totals (Categories 1, 3, 9, 11) were provided in the context; only descriptions of methodology and category definitions were given. No water quality data (e.g., pollutant concentrations in discharges), biodiversity impact assessments, or detailed TCFD risk categorisation (e.g., physical vs transition risks) were disclosed. No waste-related targets beyond plastics packaging (30% recycled content by 2030) were specified.

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures in 2025, with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025, unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) was 1.2 per million working hours in 2025 (versus 1.1 in 2024), and lost time injury frequency (LTIF) was 0.6 per million working hours (versus 0.5 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Cases of recordable work-related ill health totalled 117 in 2025, down from 262 in 2024, yielding a total recordable occupational illness frequency (TROIF) of 0.3 per million working hours (versus 0.6 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 and Mode 2 contract arrangements—where Shell retains control or shared interface management—but exclude Mode 3 contractors unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. Shell uses IOGP-defined FPI and FPI-F metrics to focus investigations on the most serious incidents and drive prevention of fatalities and permanent impairments [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974]. No quantitative data on mental health programme reach, occupational disease incidence (e.g., hearing loss, respiratory conditions), or exposure monitoring are disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_265].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This reflects a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily due to lower employee numbers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. Training supports skill development aligned with traditional and emerging business needs, including leadership development and coaching for executives [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260]. Ethics and compliance training—including mandatory Code of Conduct training—is required for all employees and contractor staff [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. For roles at higher risk of corruption or bribery, 98% of staff held valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training as of 2025 (consistent with 98% in 2024); validity is verified through tracked completion against defined two- to three-year refresh cycles, though the total number of staff in scope is not disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No data on training hours per employee, completion rates for non-ethics mandatory courses (e.g., health and safety, technical upskilling), or disaggregation by topic or duration is provided [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263].

### Diversity  
As of December 31, 2025, women comprised 35% of Shell’s total workforce of 85,000 employees [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Women represented 42% of the Board of Directors and 44% of the Executive Committee [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. In senior leadership positions (defined by compensation grade), women accounted for 35%—meeting Shell’s 2025 target—and the company aims for 40% by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. Ethnic minority representation in UK-based Senior Management stood at 16% in 2025, exceeding the Parker Review’s 15% target ahead of schedule; Shell now targets 17% by 2027 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. The Board included three Directors from minority ethnic backgrounds as of December 31, 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_495]. No data on disability inclusion, LGBT+ representation, or intersectional diversity (e.g., gender and ethnicity combined) is disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378].

### Supplier Social Assessment  
Shell’s Supplier Principles require suppliers to uphold human rights—including freedom of association, elimination of forced and child labour, non-discrimination, safe working conditions, and fair wages—and to provide confidential grievance mechanisms for workers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_929]. Risk-based pre-contractual screening assesses supplier capacity to meet these expectations, and contracts require suppliers to flow down equivalent standards to their direct suppliers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. In 2025, no cases of non-respect of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines were identified in Shell’s upstream or downstream value chain [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. Additionally, no severe human rights incidents related to value chain workers were identified in 2025 (compared to three in 2024); this finding reflects internal identification processes, as no mention of third-party audits or external verification is made in the source material [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939]. Quantitative details on supplier assessments conducted (e.g., number screened, percentage audited, or findings by risk category) are not reported [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930].

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures in 2025, with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025, unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) was 1.2 per million working hours in 2025 (versus 1.1 in 2024), and lost time injury frequency (LTIF) was 0.6 per million working hours (versus 0.5 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Cases of recordable work-related ill health totalled 117 in 2025, down from 262 in 2024, yielding a total recordable occupational illness frequency (TROIF) of 0.3 per million working hours (versus 0.6 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 and Mode 2 contract arrangements—where Shell retains control or shared interface management—but exclude Mode 3 contractors unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. Shell uses IOGP-defined FPI and FPI-F metrics to focus investigations on the most serious incidents and drive prevention of fatalities and permanent impairments [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974]. No quantitative data on mental health programme reach, occupational disease incidence (e.g., hearing loss, respiratory conditions), or exposure monitoring are disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_265].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This reflects a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily due to lower employee numbers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. Training supports skill development aligned with traditional and emerging business needs, including leadership development and coaching for executives [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260]. Ethics and compliance training—including mandatory Code of Conduct training—is required for all employees and contractor staff [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. For roles at higher risk of corruption or bribery, 98% of staff held valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training as of 2025 (consistent with 98% in 2024); validity is verified through tracked completion against defined two- to three-year refresh cycles, though the total number of staff in scope is not disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No data on training hours per employee, completion rates for non-ethics mandatory courses (e.g., health and safety, technical upskilling), or disaggregation by topic or duration is provided [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263].

### Diversity  
As of December 31, 2025, women comprised 35% of Shell’s total workforce of 85,000 employees [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_921]. Women represented 42% of the Board of Directors and 44% of the Executive Committee [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. In senior leadership positions (defined by compensation grade), women accounted for 35%—meeting Shell’s 2025 target—and the company aims for 40% by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_267]. Ethnic minority representation in UK-based Senior Management stood at 16% in 2025, exceeding the Parker Review’s 15% target ahead of schedule; Shell now targets 17% by 2027 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268]. The Board included three Directors from minority ethnic backgrounds as of December 31, 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_268][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_495]. No data on disability inclusion, LGBT+ representation, or intersectional diversity (e.g., gender and ethnicity combined) is disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_378].

### Supplier Social Assessment  
Shell’s Supplier Principles require suppliers to uphold human rights—including freedom of association, elimination of forced and child labour, non-discrimination, safe working conditions, and fair wages—and to provide confidential grievance mechanisms for workers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_929]. Risk-based pre-contractual screening assesses supplier capacity to meet these expectations, and contracts require suppliers to flow down equivalent standards to their direct suppliers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. In 2025, no cases of non-respect of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, ILO Declaration, or OECD Guidelines were identified in Shell’s upstream or downstream value chain [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930]. Additionally, no severe human rights incidents related to value chain workers were identified in 2025 (compared to three in 2024); this finding reflects internal identification processes, as no mention of third-party audits or external verification is made in the source material [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_939]. Quantitative details on supplier assessments conducted (e.g., number screened, percentage audited, or findings by risk category) are not reported [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_930].

### Not covered in source material  
GRI 403: Specific occupational health metrics beyond safety—including work-related illnesses by diagnosis, mental health programme participation rates, or exposure monitoring data—are not disclosed.  
GRI 404: Training hours per employee, % completion rates for non-ethics mandatory courses (e.g., health and safety, technical skills), and breakdown of training content by function or seniority are absent.  
GRI 405: Data on disability inclusion, LGBT+ representation, and intersectional diversity (e.g., gender and ethnicity combined) are not provided.  
GRI 414: No figures on the number of suppliers assessed, audited, or found non-compliant; nor any categorisation of assessments by risk level or geography.  
TCFD Strategy (social impacts of climate transition): No analysis of workforce transitions, reskilling for low-carbon roles, social impacts of portfolio changes (e.g., divestments in Nigeria, UK, Singapore), or just transition commitments is included in the context.

### Governance Structure and Board Oversight  
Shell plc’s governance framework is structured around the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee (EC), with the Board comprising 12 members—including two executive and 10 non-executive directors—as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 12 members, 2 executive and 10 non-executive members) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. All non-executive directors are considered independent in character and judgement, representing 83% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 83%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Board maintains primary oversight of Shell’s strategy—including its Energy Transition Strategy 2024, endorsed in March 2024—and monitors performance against longer-term business targets, including climate-related ambitions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Sustainability matters, including climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, are reviewed and addressed on an integrated basis alongside other business issues throughout the year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. The Board delegates authority for operational management to the CEO, who chairs the EC and is supported by EC members in implementing strategy and monitoring progress [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. The Sustainability Committee oversees emerging sustainability trends excluding carbon and safety; the Carbon Reporting Committee governs GHG emissions calculation and external disclosures; and the Sustainability Management Committee drives cross-business integration of sustainability objectives—including climate-related opportunities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242].

### Board Diversity, Composition and Succession  
Shell’s Board Diversity Policy—first published in March 2024—commits to gender balance, with women constituting 42% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 42%), corresponding to a female-to-male ratio of 0.7 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The target to maintain representation of both men and women at or above 40% was set in 2024, with the 2023 baseline not disclosed in the source material [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. Shell also aims to maintain or exceed having at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background, though no baseline year or deadline (e.g., “by 2027”) is specified in the context [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The Nomination and Succession Committee (NOMCO) oversees development of a diverse pipeline for Board succession and ensures all appointments follow a formal, rigorous and transparent procedure based on merit and objective criteria, with due regard for diversity factors [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. NOMCO engages independent executive search consultants aligned with Shell’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) approach to identify candidates from diverse pools [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379].

### Ethics, Compliance and Anti-Corruption Governance  
Accountability for ethics and compliance rests with the CEO and the Executive Committee, supported by the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO), who reports to the Chief Legal Officer and provides updates to the EC and Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Shell’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption programme includes mandatory Code of Conduct training for all employees and contractor staff, with targeted, risk-based training for roles involving procurement, government engagement or new business development [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. In 2025, 98% of staff in at-risk roles possessed valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training completion (2024: 98%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No Shell legal entity nor, to the best of Shell’s knowledge, any Shell staff were convicted or fined for criminal violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws in 2025 (2024: no convictions or fines) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961]. Breaches may be reported confidentially—including anonymously—via the Shell Global Helpline; in 2025, 1,983 reports were received [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. Shell maintains a stringent no-retaliation policy for good-faith reporters and those involved in investigations [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_956]. The context does not disclose whether the anti-corruption programme—including training completion rates or Helpline operations—underwent external assurance, nor does it specify a target for % of Helpline reports resolved within 90 days, including a 2025 baseline or 2027 deadline [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961].

### Climate and Sustainability Risk Governance  
Climate change and the energy transition are identified as material strategic risks, with sub-components including commercial, societal (including litigation), regulatory and physical risks [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168]. The ARC assists the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities for risk management and internal control, including ethics and compliance-related matters [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Each business and function regularly reviews its risk profile and assurance activities to ensure climate-related risks are effectively managed, with insights informing operational decisions and risk response plans [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_783]. The context does not disclose political contributions or lobbying expenditures for 2025, nor their recipients, as required under GRI 205-3 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961].

### Not covered in source material  
The provided context does not disclose: (i) total monetary value or recipients of political contributions and lobbying expenditures in 2025 (GRI 205-3); (ii) whether anti-corruption disclosures—including training completion rates or Shell Global Helpline operations—were subject to external assurance, nor the name of the assurer or scope of work (GRI 205-1, GRI 2-12); (iii) a baseline year or value for the 40%+ gender representation target (e.g., “2023 baseline of 33%”); (iv) a deadline or baseline for the commitment to “at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background”; (v) a target for % of Helpline reports resolved within 90 days, including a 2025 baseline and 2027 deadline; (vi) third-party assurance scope or findings for governance disclosures; (vii) board-level oversight of cyber-risk or data privacy governance; (viii) detailed breakdown of committee mandates beyond high-level descriptions.

### Governance Structure and Board Oversight  
Shell plc’s governance framework is structured around the Board of Directors and the Executive Committee (EC), with the Board comprising 12 members—including two executive and 10 non-executive directors—as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 12 members, 2 executive and 10 non-executive members) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. All non-executive directors are considered independent in character and judgement, representing 83% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 83%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Board maintains primary oversight of Shell’s strategy—including its Energy Transition Strategy 2024, endorsed in March 2024—and monitors performance against longer-term business targets, including climate-related ambitions [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Sustainability matters, including climate-related impacts, risks and opportunities, are reviewed and addressed on an integrated basis alongside other business issues throughout the year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. The Board delegates authority for operational management to the CEO, who chairs the EC and is supported by EC members in implementing strategy and monitoring progress [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242].

### Board Diversity, Composition and Succession  
Shell’s Board Diversity Policy—first published in March 2024—commits to gender balance, with women constituting 42% of the Board as at December 31, 2025 (2024: 42%), corresponding to a female-to-male ratio of 0.7 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_757]. The Policy sets a target to maintain representation of both men and women at or above 40%, and aims to have at least one senior Board position (Chair, CEO, Senior Independent Director or CFO) held by a woman [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. Shell also aims to maintain or exceed having at least one Board member from a minority ethnic background [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_376]. The Nomination and Succession Committee (NOMCO) oversees development of a diverse pipeline for Board succession and ensures all appointments follow a formal, rigorous and transparent procedure based on merit and objective criteria, with due regard for diversity factors [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379]. NOMCO engages independent executive search consultants aligned with Shell’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DE&I) approach to identify candidates from diverse pools [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_379].

### Ethics, Compliance and Anti-Corruption Governance  
Accountability for ethics and compliance rests with the CEO and the Executive Committee, supported by the Chief Ethics and Compliance Officer (CECO), who reports to the Chief Legal Officer and provides updates to the EC and Audit and Risk Committee (ARC) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Shell’s anti-bribery and anti-corruption programme includes mandatory Code of Conduct training for all employees and contractor staff, with targeted, risk-based training for roles involving procurement, government engagement or new business development [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. In 2025, 98% of staff in at-risk roles possessed valid anti-bribery and anti-corruption training completion (2024: 98%) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_960]. No Shell legal entity nor, to the best of Shell’s knowledge, any Shell staff were convicted or fined for criminal violations of anti-corruption and anti-bribery laws in 2025 (2024: no convictions or fines) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_961]. Breaches may be reported confidentially—including anonymously—via the Shell Global Helpline; in 2025, 1,983 reports were received [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284]. Shell maintains a stringent no-retaliation policy for good-faith reporters and those involved in investigations [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_284][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_956].

### Climate and Sustainability Risk Governance  
Climate change and the energy transition are identified as material strategic risks, with sub-components including commercial, societal (including litigation), regulatory and physical risks [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_168]. The Board oversees climate-related risk management through dedicated structures: the Sustainability Committee addresses emerging sustainability trends (excluding carbon and safety); the Audit and Risk Committee reviews risk management effectiveness and internal controls; the Carbon Reporting Committee governs GHG emissions calculation and external disclosures; and the Sustainability Management Committee drives cross-business integration of sustainability objectives [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242]. The ARC assists the Board in fulfilling its responsibilities for risk management and internal control, including ethics and compliance-related matters [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_759]. Each business and function regularly reviews its risk profile and assurance activities to ensure climate-related risks are effectively managed, with insights informing operational decisions and risk response plans [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_242][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_783].

### Not covered in source material  
The provided context does not disclose: (i) specific quantitative metrics on Board meeting attendance or frequency; (ii) details of Board evaluation methodology beyond composition reviews; (iii) remuneration-linked ESG performance metrics for non-Executive Directors; (iv) third-party assurance scope or findings for governance disclosures; (v) board-level oversight of cyber-risk or data privacy governance; (vi) disclosure of political contributions or lobbying expenditures; (vii) detailed breakdown of committee mandates beyond high-level descriptions; (viii) whistleblower case resolution rates or investigation timelines.

Environmental.draft:
### GRI 302 Energy  
Shell’s total energy consumption in 2025 was 269 million MWh, down from 289 million MWh in 2024, primarily due to portfolio changes and greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement and transformation projects [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Of this, 189 million MWh was consumed from facilities under Shell’s operational control, with 187 million MWh (99%) sourced from fossil fuels — comprising 40 million MWh from crude oil and petroleum products, 108 million MWh from natural gas, 10 million MWh from other fossil sources, and 28 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from fossil sources [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Renewable energy consumption from facilities under operational control amounted to 2.6 million MWh in 2025, including 2.4 million MWh from purchased or acquired electricity, heat, steam and cooling from renewable sources [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_829]. Energy intensity per net revenue was 0.001 MWh/$ in both 2024 and 2025, though Shell notes this metric is not considered reliable for cross-entity or longitudinal comparison due to boundary misalignment between energy consumption (ESRS reporting boundary) and net revenue (financial control boundary) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_828].

### GRI 303 Water  
Water consumption reported against the operational control boundary was 86 million cubic metres in 2025, down from 90 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_878]. Of this, approximately 72 million cubic metres (84%) was used for manufacturing oil products and chemicals, and 13 million cubic metres for oil and gas production [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_870]. In 2025, Shell consumed 8 million cubic metres of water in areas of high water stress, a reduction from 21 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Water recycled and reused totalled 25 million cubic metres in 2025, up from 23 million cubic metres in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Shell retired its prior commitment to reduce fresh water consumption in water-stressed areas, having achieved it ahead of schedule in 2022; the commitment formally ended in December 2025 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_876].

### GRI 305 Emissions  
Shell’s gross Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions (net of carbon credits) were 53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025, compared with 58 million tonnes CO₂e in 2024 and 83 million tonnes CO₂e in the 2016 baseline year [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_204][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. This represents a 36% net reduction since 2016 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29]. The 2025 reduction was driven by divestments (4.8 million tonnes), emission-reduction activities and renewable electricity purchases (1.2 million tonnes), and changes in output (0.1 million tonnes), partially offset by acquisitions (1.4 million tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1098]. Methane emissions intensity for Shell-operated oil and gas assets with marketed gas was 0.04% in 2025, well below the 0.2% target and trending toward near-zero by 2030 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119]. Routine flaring from upstream operations was eliminated in January 2025, independent of the March 2025 sale of SPDC [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165].

### GRI 306 Waste  
In 2025, Shell generated 3,239 thousand tonnes of waste, down from 3,452 thousand tonnes in 2024 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Hazardous waste totalled 822 thousand tonnes (2024: 1,104 thousand tonnes), of which 615 thousand tonnes was directed to disposal (2024: 695 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_985]. Non-hazardous waste disposed was 1,533 thousand tonnes in 2025 (2024: 1,396 thousand tonnes), while hazardous waste disposed decreased to 454 thousand tonnes (2024: 536 thousand tonnes) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Total waste diverted from disposal was 403 thousand tonnes in 2025, down from 728 thousand tonnes in 2024 — a decline attributed to changes in waste classification and reporting methodology [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_906]. Initiatives included using drilling waste in cement and lubricant production in Malaysia, trialling bio-sludge for soil enhancement in Qatar, and returning unused chemicals to suppliers in the Gulf of America [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_278][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_900].

### TCFD Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics & Targets  
Shell’s climate strategy is anchored in its ambition to become a net-zero emissions energy business by 2050 (Scope 1, 2 and 3), with interim targets aligned to a 1.5°C pathway derived from IPCC AR6 scenarios [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_222][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_165]. Key metrics include net Scope 1 and 2 emissions (53 million tonnes CO₂e in 2025), methane intensity (0.04% in 2025), routine flaring (eliminated in 2025), and Net Carbon Intensity (NCI) — reduced by 9.0% versus the 2016 baseline of 78 gCO₂e/MJ [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_1119][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440]. Risk management integrates portfolio changes, abatement projects (e.g., CCS, electrification), and regulatory compliance, with carbon credits permitted only after avoidance and reduction, per the carbon mitigation hierarchy [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_223]. Targets are embedded in executive remuneration, including methane intensity and NCI performance [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_29][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_440].

### Not covered in source material  
No quantitative data on Scope 3 emissions totals (Categories 1, 3, 9, 11) were provided in the context; only descriptions of methodology and category definitions were given. No water quality data (e.g., pollutant concentrations in discharges), biodiversity impact assessments, or detailed TCFD risk categorisation (e.g., physical vs transition risks) were disclosed. No waste-related targets beyond plastics packaging (30% recycled content by 2030) were specified.

### Occupational Health & Safety  
Shell reported 4 fatalities among contractor colleagues in Shell-operated ventures in 2025, with no employee fatalities [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. The fatality and permanent impairment (FPI) count was 8 in 2025, unchanged from the revised 2024 figure of 8 [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Total recordable case frequency (TRCF) was 1.2 per million working hours in 2025 (versus 1.1 in 2024), and lost time injury frequency (LTIF) was 0.6 per million working hours (versus 0.5 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. Cases of recordable work-related ill health totalled 117 in 2025, down from 262 in 2024, yielding a total recordable occupational illness frequency (TROIF) of 0.3 per million working hours (versus 0.6 in 2024) [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_973]. These metrics cover employees and contractors under Mode 1 and Mode 2 contract arrangements—where Shell retains control or shared interface management—but exclude Mode 3 contractors unless working on Shell premises [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_975]. Shell uses IOGP-defined FPI and FPI-F metrics to focus investigations on the most serious incidents and drive prevention of fatalities and permanent impairments [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_974]. No quantitative data on mental health programme reach, occupational disease incidence (e.g., hearing loss, respiratory conditions), or exposure monitoring are disclosed [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_265].

### Training  
In 2025, Shell delivered 253,000 formal training days to employees and joint-venture partners [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_260][shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263]. This reflects a reduction from 264,000 training days in 2024, primarily due to lower employee numbers [shell-integrated-annual-and-sustainability-report_chunk_263].
